chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'We have a young girl who used to see the planet like a jar.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and she sees it like a grain.' I said: 'Her eyesight is weak.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Apply kohl to her eyes with the Sabr (a type of shrub), Myrrh, and Camphor in equal parts.' So we applied it to her, and it benefited her.

key_terms.الصَّبِر: Sabr (a medicinal shrub, often interpreted as a type of myrrh or similar resinous plant)
key_terms.الكَوْكَب: Planet (often referring to Venus or a bright star, here used metaphorically for a small object)

ai.seo_question: What was the prescribed treatment for weak eyesight in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of *Tibb al-Nabawi* (Prophetic Medicine) through Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who prescribed a balanced mixture of Sabr (Acacia gum), Myrrh, and Camphor as eye kohl to treat a young girl's weakened vision. It highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of integrating spiritual and physical healing, demonstrating that the Imams provided specific, effective medical remedies using readily available natural substances. The success of this treatment underscores the belief in the Imams' comprehensive knowledge of both religious law and the medicinal properties of the natural world.

en.hubeali: H 15028 – From him, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Salih who said:

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws that. ‘We have a young girl who used to see the planet like the jar’. Heasws said: ‘Yes, and she can see it like a grain’. So I said, ‘Her eyesight is weak’. So heasws said: ‘Apply (in her eyes) the Aloe, and the Myrrh, and the Camphor in equal parts’. So we applied it in her eyes, and she benefited from it’.
en.sarwar: 582. From him, from Ahmad, from Dawood Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Al-Fayz, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said: ‘I (a.s.) was in the presence of Abu Ja’far, meaning Abu Al-Dawaniq, when a packet came and he opened it and looked inside it. So he took something out from it. He said, ‘O Abu Abdullah (a.s.), do you (a.s.) know what this is?’ I (a.s.) said: ‘What is it?’ He said, ‘This is something that has come to me from behind Africa, from Tanjat, (or Tabnat, Muhammad (the narrator doubted).

So I (a.s.) said: ‘What is it?’ He said, ‘There is a mountain there from which drops come out in a year and solidify, and it is best for the whiteness which occurs in the eyes, if this is applied to them, it would go away by the Permission of Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic. I (a.s.) said, ‘Yes, I recognise it, and if you like I can inform you of its name and its condition’. He (a.s.) said: ‘He never asked me (a.s.) about its name’. He said, ‘And what is its condition?’ So I (a.s.) said: ‘This is a mountain on which was a Prophet (as) from the sons of the Children of Israel, who had fled from his (as) people, and he (as) used to worship upon it. So the people came to know about it, and they killed him. So it (mountain) now weeps over that Prophet (as), and these are the drops from its weeping. And on the other side of it is a spring from which the water flows by the night and the day, but it does not arrive to that fountain (of tears)’.
